drivingQuestion: May repulsive matter be removed, and may one create such a situation deliberately?
outcomeNote: the inference that filth may be removed only with its vessel is refuted by Rav Ashi's practice

segments.he: בֵּי רִחְיָא דְּאַבָּיֵי דְּלוּף. אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל עַיְּילֵיהּ לְפוּרְיָךְ לְהָתָם, דְּלֶהֱוֵי כִּגְרָף שֶׁל רְעִי, וְאַפְּקֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «Abaye’s millhouse» once «developed a leak» on Shabbat. Abaye was concerned about the potential damage to the millstones, which were made partly of clay and which would become ruined from the leaking water, and he did not have enough buckets to catch all the water without emptying and refilling them. But the water was unfit for drinking and was therefore muktze and could not be removed. Abaye «came before Rabba» to ask him how to proceed. Rabba «said to him: Go» and «bring your bed into» the millhouse, «so that» the dirty water «will be» considered «like a container of excrement,» which, despite being muktze, may be removed from one’s presence due to its repulsive nature, «and» then «remove» the water.

segments.he: יָתֵיב אַבָּיֵי וְקָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ: וְכִי עוֹשִׂין גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי לְכַתְּחִלָּה? אַדְּהָכִי נְפַל בֵּי רִחְיָא דְאַבָּיֵי. אָמַר: תֵּיתֵי לִי דַּעֲבַרִי אַדְּמַר.
segments.en: «Abaye sat» and examined the matter «and posed a difficulty: And may one initiate» a situation of «a container of excrement,» i.e., may one intentionally place any repulsive matter into a situation which will bother him and will then have to be removed, «ab initio? In the meantime,» as he was deliberating the issue, «Abaye’s millhouse collapsed. He said: I had» this «coming to me for having gone against the words of my master,» Rabba, by not following his ruling unquestioningly.

segments.he: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי וְעָבִיט שֶׁל מֵימֵי רַגְלַיִם — מוּתָּר לְהוֹצִיאָן לָאַשְׁפָּה, וּכְשֶׁהוּא מַחְזִירוֹ — נוֹתֵן בּוֹ מַיִם וּמַחְזִירוֹ.
segments.en: «Shmuel said:» With regard to «a container of excrement and a container of urine, it is permitted to remove them» on Shabbat «to a garbage heap. And when he returns» the container to the house «he must place water in it» first «and» then «return it,» for it is prohibited to carry these containers alone, as their foul odor makes them muktze due to their repulsive nature.

segments.he: סְבוּר מִינַּהּ: גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי, אַגַּב מָנָא — אִין, בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ — לָא. תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּהָהוּא עַכְבַּרְתָּא דְּאִשְׁתְּכַח בֵּי אִסְפַּרְמָקֵי דְּרַב אָשֵׁי. אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב אָשֵׁי: נִקְטֻהּ בְּצוּצִיתֵהּ וְאַפְּקוּהּ.
segments.en: Some Sages at first «understood from» the wording of Shmuel’s statement that with regard to removing «a container of excrement on account of the vessel,» i.e., along with its vessel: «Yes,» this is permitted; but to remove the excrement «by itself,» without a vessel containing it: «No,» this is prohibited. The Gemara counters this conclusion with the following story: «Come» and «hear that a certain» dead «mouse was discovered in Rav Ashi’s storeroom» for «spices» [«isparmekei»]. «Rav Ashi said to them: Take hold of it by its tail and remove it.» This shows that repulsive matter may be removed even directly.
